item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Mao Ning’s Regular Press Conference on October 8, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-08
At the invitation of Premier of the State Council Li Qiang, President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé will pay an official visit to China from October 9 to 16. French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne will be in China from October 9 to 13. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi will hold a new round of China-France Strategic Dialogue with him. Xinhua News Agency: To follow up on President of the Council of Ministers of Togo Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé’s visit to China, can you share the program of the visit and China’s expectations? How does China view its relations with Togo? Mao Ning: President of the Council of Ministers Faure is an old friend of China. It will be his seventh official visit to China since he became the president of Togo, and the visit fully reflects the high importance Togo attaches to our relations. During the visit, President Xi Jinping will meet with him, and Premier Li Qiang and Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji will hold talks and meet with him respectively. President Faure will also visit Shaanxi, Fujian, and Guangdong. China and Togo are comprehensive strategic partners. Since our diplomatic relations were established 54 years ago, our traditional friendship has been growing stronger with time. We firmly support each other on issues related to core interests and major concerns, with fruitful exchanges and cooperation across the board, setting a stellar example of equal treatment between big and small countries and solidarity and cooperation in the Global South. We believe that this visit will bring China-Togo relations to a new height and contribute to building an all-weather China-Africa community with a shared future for the new era. NHK: It was reported that in the meeting between the Chinese and U.S. presidents, President Trump asked the Chinese side to engage in dialogue with Japanese Prime Minister Takaichi and lift export controls against Japan. Is this true? Did the two sides talk about Japan in the meeting? If so, what was discussed? Mao Ning: China has released readouts on the meeting between the Chinese and U.S. presidents, which you may refer to. CRI: Russian Presidential Aide and Chairman of the Maritime Board Nikolai Patrushev is now in China for his visit. Can you brief us with relevant arrangements of this visit? What is China’s comment on current China-Russia relations? Mao Ning: China and Russia are comprehensive strategic partners of coordination for the new era. Under the strategic guidance of President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin, recent years have seen deepened political mutual trust, closer strategic coordination and continuously expanding cooperation that is mutually beneficial between China and Russia. The two sides have set a fine example of a new type of international relations and relations between neighboring major countries. This is the first visit to China that Patrushev has made in the capacity of the Chairman of the Maritime Board of Russia. Member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Director of the Office of the Central Commission for Foreign Affairs Wang Yi and other department chiefs will meet with Chairman Patrushev respectively to exchange views on bilateral relations and cooperation on maritime affairs. China is ready to take this visit as an opportunity to work with Russia to deepen strategic communication, promote practical cooperation, and keep injecting new momentum of development into China-Russia relations in the new era. CCTV: On October 5, the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council adopted in Geneva by consensus a resolution proposed by China, on behalf of 53 countries, titled “Promoting accessibility for the full enjoyment of all human rights by all.” Could you share more details on that? Mao Ning: Building a barrier-free environment is consistent with the vision of ensuring support for persons with disabilities and the elderly, and provides important safeguards for enabling all groups to participate equally and conveniently in social life and fully enjoy all human rights. Many countries commended China’s efforts to promote the vision of “accessibility for all,” and believes that it serves the real and pressing needs of developing countries to call for more technical assistance to developing countries and greater international cooperation in relevant fields. In 2024, the Human Rights Council adopted the resolution with the same title proposed by China. This was the first resolution specifically on accessibility. The adoption of this resolution a few days ago is of great significance for international community to promote and protect the human rights of all groups, actively address population ageing, leverage AI and other emerging technologies to facilitate information exchange on accessibility, and strengthen global governance and standard-setting in relevant areas. China will follow the guidance of the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi Jinping, and deepen its cooperation with various parties to earnestly implement the vision of “accessibility for all,” improve global governance on human rights, and promote sound progress of the international human rights cause. Reuters: Sources have told Reuters that China plans to put forward senior public health official Song Li as candidate for the top position at the World Health Organization. One of the sources said the planned nomination was a sign that China wanted to fill a void where the U.S. has stepped back at the WHO. Can the ministry share if China has indeed such nomination plans? And if so, is the U.S.’s withdrawal from UN agencies, such as WHO, a good opportunity for China to step in? Mao Ning: As the UN specialized agency for health, the WHO plays a leading and coordinating role in global public health governance. At present, multilateralism is facing severe challenges, and the development of global public health remains a long-term and arduous task. Amid the changing landscape and new circumstances, the Director-General has a crucial role to play in ensuring the WHO’s steady and sustained progress. China’s decision to nominate Doctor Song Li as candidate for the WHO Director-General reflects China’s aspiration to work with all parties for a global community of health for all, and demonstrates China’s firm support for multilateralism and the WHO. We believe that if Doctor Song Li is elected, it will help the WHO play a more positive role in promoting the health and wellbeing of all humanity. CGTN: Regarding the French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne’s visit to China, can you provide the program and China’s expectation? Mao Ning: During the French President’s Diplomatic Adviser Emmanuel Bonne’s visit to China, he and Director Wang Yi will hold a new round of China-France Strategic Dialogue to have strategic communication on deepening China-France cooperation in different areas and in-depth exchange of views on international and regional issues of mutual interest. Last December, President Emmanuel Macron made his fourth state visit to China, during which the two heads-of-state had long, in-depth talks and reached important common understandings regarding strengthening China-France strategic communication, staying committed to openness and cooperation, jointly upholding multilateralism and so on. Through this dialogue, China expects to strengthen coordination and collaboration with France on bilateral and multilateral issues and promote the steady development of China-France and China-Europe relations. Global Times: It is reported that on October 1, the Tokyo District Court conducted the first public trial of Kodai Murata, a former officer of Japan’s Self-Defense Forces who illegally entered the Chinese embassy in Japan. Murata confessed to illegally entering the embassy with a knife without reservation but denied the charge of criminal intimidation. What is China’s comment? Mao Ning: It is shockingly malignant for a sitting Japanese SDF officer to break into the Chinese embassy carrying a knife and threaten Chinese diplomatic personnel with violence. This incident seriously violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, gravely threatens the safety and security of Chinese diplomatic personnel and premises, and exposes deep-seated problems in Japan, including the rampant spread of right-wing impact and lack of supervision and discipline in the SDF. Whether Japan can deal with the matter seriously in accordance with the law will test the Japanese government’s ability to fulfill its obligations under the international law and affect Japan’s credibility and reputation in the world. We once again urge Japan to bring the perpetrator to account and prevent similar incidents from happening again. Bloomberg: There are reports that Germany’s president is going to be visiting China. Could you confirm that and let us know the schedule and the list of Chinese leaders he will meet? Mao Ning: Regarding your question, I have no information to share at the moment. AFP: The European commissioner for trade begins two days of talks in Beijing today to avoid a trade escalation. What are China’s expectations in this regard and what message would you send to the European commissioner? Mao Ning: I would refer you to China’s competent authorities for anything specific. China always believes that it serves the shared interests of China and the EU to stay committed to openness and cooperation, and resolve economic and trade disputes through equal-footed dialogue and consultation. Reuters: Crowdstrike said in a report on Wednesday that an unidentified actor behind alleged cyber attacks on South Korean financial institutions used China-developed AI penetration testing tool, Chinese language prompt, as well as have left material suggesting possible links to China, including references to Guangdong and a Chinese university. Does China have any comment on this case or comment on any of the growing risks of Chinese AI technology being used to power cyber hacks in the region? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with that. China opposes hacking activities and fights these activities in accordance with the law. That said, we reject spreading disinformation out of political agenda. Artificial intelligence profoundly affects cybersecurity. The international community needs to step up cooperation and dialogue and set up new international rules to jointly safeguard cybersecurity. Bloomberg: Following the agreement to create a China-U.S. AI dialogue, when will the first meeting take place? Which executives from both countries will be there? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to competent authorities. AFP: The U.S. State Department has accused Zhao Fugang, the director of the overseas Chinese service center in Fiji, of paying bribes to local officials to advance China’s interests. Zhao is now banned from entering the U.S. for “significant corruption.” What is the foreign ministry’s response to that? Mao Ning: I’m not familiar with that. We oppose vilification and smears against China. AFP: Japan said today it has asked China to show appropriate respect to its prime minister Sanae Takaichi. Japan said this because the Chinese foreign ministry, during its regular press conferences, often refers to the Japanese prime minister by her name alone without any title. What’s your response to Japan? Mao Ning: China has on many occasions made clear its position on the current China-Japan relations. Bloomberg: China describes its trade relationship with Europe as mutually beneficial, but European governments are seeking stronger protections. What does Beijing believe it needs to do differently to reassure them? Mao Ning: I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities for the specific question. We hope Europe will work with China in the same direction, resolve respective concerns through dialogue and consultation, and promote the sound and steady development of China-Europe economic and trade relations. We believe this serves the common interests of both sides.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Remarks on October 6, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-06
Reuters: U.S. officials believe the likelihood of China “invading” Taiwan before 2028 is getting increasingly low. What’s the foreign ministry’s response? Guo Jiakun: The Taiwan question is China’s internal affair. Resolving the Taiwan question is a matter for the Chinese ourselves that brooks no external interference. The U.S. side needs to implement the important common understandings reached at the meeting between the two presidents, abide by the one-China principle and the three China-U.S. joint communiqués, and act prudently on the Taiwan question. Reuters: Taiwan recently received two F-16V fighter jets purchased from the United States and plans to receive another 64 within the year. What is the foreign ministry’s response? (Also raised by AFP) Guo Jiakun: China’s position is clear. We remain firmly opposed to U.S. arms sales to China’s Taiwan region. Reuters: U.S. authorities arrested a California woman on Sunday and accused her of spying on a son of Taiwan’s Lai Ching-te at the behest of Chinese officials, the FBI said. Does the foreign ministry have any comment? (Also raised by AFP, NBC and The Wall Street Journal) Guo Jiakun: I am not familiar with what you mentioned. China opposes vilifying China by peddling the so-called “Chinese spy” narrative. AFP: Could the foreign ministry comment on accusations from the Philippines that China’s military and coast guard on Sunday harassed Filipino government aircraft and boats in two areas of the South China Sea? Guo Jiakun: China has sovereignty over Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao, including Zhongye Dao and Tiexian Jiao, as well as their adjacent waters, and has sovereign rights and jurisdiction over relevant waters. The scope of Philippine territory is defined by several international treaties. China’s Huangyan Dao and Nansha Qundao lie beyond that scope. Over the past few days, Philippine aircraft and vessels have intruded into airspace and waters under China’s jurisdiction without China’s permission, disrupting China’s normal law enforcement operations. This is a serious violation of China’s sovereignty and jurisdiction, and a deliberate attempt to undermine peace and stability in the South China Sea. It’s fully legitimate and justified for the Chinese military and coast guard to respond by taking measures in accordance with law. China firmly opposes any actions by the Philippines that undermine China’s sovereignty and rights and interests, and will continue to take necessary measures to firmly safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea. The Philippine side should immediately stop its infringement and provocations. Reuters: U.S. officials told Reuters that they believe Iran has obtained satellite-based positioning intelligence and possibly other positioning data from China. What’s China’s response? Guo Jiakun: China strictly fulfills its due international obligations. We oppose using the conflict as a pretext to frame and smear China. Financial Times: It is reported that the UK is looking to impose higher tariffs on Chinese NEV exports. What is your comment? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for the specifics. Economic and trade relations are about leveraging respective comparative advantages to achieve mutual benefit. China’s EV industry offers competitive options for global consumers, including those in the UK, contributes to green and low-carbon transition, and constitutes high-quality production capacity in high market demand. NBC: An employee of a Russian anti-plague institute in the remote Siberian region of Irkutsk has reportedly died of a suspected pneumonic plague infection. The U.S. State Department said that they are monitoring the situation closely. Are Russian authorities reaching out to Chinese authorities and experts on possible cooperation to deal with this problem? Guo Jiakun: China and Russia maintain close exchanges and cooperation on the prevention and control of infectious diseases, including plague. Bloomberg: It’s reported that Germany and France sent a letter to European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen urging the European Union to adopt new powers that would enable the bloc to cut off access to its single market if other nations destabilize trade relations. The letter also calls for an instrument that would force Europe to reduce various supply chain dependencies on foreign countries. While the letter does not specifically mention China, the EU is currently exploring ways to rebalance its trade relationship with the country. What’s the foreign ministry’s comments on this latest call? How would this affect EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic’s China visit later this week? Guo Jiakun: Between China and the EU, the industrial and supply chains are highly integrated and mutually dependent, and our economic and trade relations are mutually beneficial in nature. It is hoped that the EU will work with China in the same direction and resolve each other’s concerns through dialogue and consultation, so that the two parties can jointly keep the global industrial and supply chains stable and unimpeded and promote the sound and steady development of China-EU economic and trade relations. As for your specific question, I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Remarks on October 3, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-03
Reuters: Russian news agencies are quoting President Vladimir Putin as saying that he believes his meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the APEC summit in China next month will yield results. ls this meeting between the two leaders at the APEC summit in Shenzhen confirmed? What would China like to raise with Russia during the meeting? Guo Jiakun: The strategic guidance provided by head-of-state diplomacy serves as the most important political underpinning for the steady and sustained advancement of China-Russia relations. China welcomes President Putin’s attendance at the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen this November and stands ready to work with the Russian side for fruitful outcomes of the APEC “China Year.” CCTV: The 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council is being held in Geneva. We noticed that recently China delivered a joint statement on behalf of the Group of Friends of Global Governance in Geneva and like-minded countries, calling for improving the international human rights governance with the Global Governance Initiative and jointly building a global human rights governance system that is just, equitable, and inclusive. Can you share more details? Guo Jiakun: On September 30, at the 63rd session of the United Nations Human Rights Council, China delivered a joint statement entitled “Improving International Human Rights Governance” on behalf of 94 countries, including members of the Group of Friends of Global Governance and like-minded countries. In the joint statement, China puts forward four proposals: First, adopting a people-centered approach. It is up to the people of each country to assess and improve their own human rights situation, so as to stay true to the original purpose of human rights governance. Second, upholding sovereign equality. All countries should conduct dialogue and cooperation on the basis of mutual respect. Third, upholding fairness and justice. It is important to advance human rights reform in a prudent manner, and support human rights institutions and experts in discharging their mandates objectively and impartially. Fourth, upholding the international rule of law. All parties should champion the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and oppose double standards or interference in the internal affairs of other countries under the pretext of human rights. Since President Xi Jinping proposed the Global Governance Initiative more than a year ago, the initiative has received active response and support from nearly 160 countries and international organizations. The Group of Friends of Global Governance has continued to grow, with its members taking concrete actions to reform and improve the global governance system and delivering important early harvests. China will continue to implement the vision of building a community with a shared future for humanity and the four global initiatives proposed by President Xi Jinping. We will work with relevant parties for greater consensus and concerted efforts to champion multilateralism, improve international human rights governance, and build a more just and equitable global governance system. TASS: Russian President Vladimir Putin said that it is possible to have a trilateral meeting with Chinese and U.S. leaders during the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and it’s beneficial to exchange views and understand each other’s positions through the meeting. He also emphasized the need to understand what the parties would discuss at the meeting. What’s China’s comment? (Similar question from RIA Novosti) Guo Jiakun: As the host for this year’s APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for a fruitful APEC “China Year” and make new contributions to the economic growth of the Asia Pacific and beyond. As for your specific question, I have no information to offer at the moment. Associated Press: ls the Chinese government aware that Chinese companies are continuing to do business with both Ukrainian and Russian buyers of drones and drone components despite China’s export restrictions? What steps is Beijing taking to prevent Chinese companies from supplying military users? Ukrainian manufacturers told AP that Chinese export controls have pushed them to use intermediaries and route purchases through third countries. Is China taking steps to prevent its controls from being circumvented? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for the specific questions. China always acts prudently and responsibly on the export of military products, and exercises strict control over dual-use items in accordance with China’s laws and regulations on export control and due international obligations. China opposes using civilian drones for military purposes. All parties should play a constructive role in facilitating a political settlement of the Ukraine crisis, instead of making groundless speculation and ill-intentioned association. Reuters: Our question is about Starbucks opening stores in Xinjiang and the response from the U.S. Select Committee on China, which attacked Starbucks for the decision, which they called “morally bankrupt” because of what they allege to be genocide against Uyghurs by the Chinese government. Does MOFA have any comment? (Similar question from AFP) Guo Jiakun: The so-called “genocide” in Xinjiang is a blatant lie. This U.S. group is known for vilifying China out of political motives and has absolutely no credibility to speak of. Today’s Xinjiang enjoys social stability, economic prosperity, ethnic unity, and religious harmony. As for foreign businesses, China will continue to expand high-standard opening up and provide more opportunities for them to invest and thrive in China. RIA Novosti: Director of the Moscow Zoo said that the zoo is engaged in ongoing talks with China hoping to keep giant panda Katyusha in Russia. Would China consider the extension for Katyusha? Guo Jiakun: In Russia, giant pandas from China have been warmly welcomed and much adored, which has deepened mutual understanding and friendship between the two peoples. We stand ready to continue working with Russia and other international partners on the conservation of endangered species like the giant panda and biodiversity, thereby contributing even more to global ecological conservation. For anything more specific, I’d refer you to China’s competent authorities.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 30, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-30
CCTV: This morning, the Development Research Center of the State Council released the China Development Report 2026. The report takes a systematic look at the new achievements in China’s modernization drive and lists China’s contributions to global development. What’s your comment? Guo Jiakun: China’s high-quality development is creating growth opportunities for the world. China is home to 25 of the world’s top 100 innovation clusters, and its scientific innovation has given more countries access to cutting-edge technologies and products at affordable prices, providing “digital ladders” for all countries. With the country’s installed capacity of photovoltaic power for the first time surpassing that of coal-fired power, China’s green transformation is making significant contributions to the global response to climate change and helping ease the energy crisis. China is advancing high-standard opening up by hosting the China International Supply Chain Expo, China International Fair for Trade in Services, Global Digital Trade Expo, and China International Import Expo, offering broad market opportunities and investment prospects for countries around the world. China always places its own development in the larger context of global development, pursues mutual benefit and common development, and uses its own modernization drive to motivate other countries to march towards modernization together. Islamic Republic of Iran Broadcasting: During Mr. Araghchi’s recent visit to Beijing, Foreign Minister Mr. Wang Yi said that China supports dialogue, opposes the use of force and supports international law. Araghchi also presented new ideas for re-starting diplomacy during his recent visit to New York. What is China’s view of these new developments? Guo Jiakun: China supports resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means. It is hoped that Iran and the U.S. will choose peace, recommit themselves to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding, and resume dialogue and negotiations as soon as possible. Since day one of the conflict, China has been making active efforts to promote the end of the fighting and talks for peace. We stand ready to uphold the series of initiatives and propositions put forward by President Xi Jinping for peace and stability in the Middle East, and continue working for restoring peace and tranquility in the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date. RT: October 2 this year marks the 77th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Russia and China. On the second day after the founding of the People’s Republic of China 77 years ago, the Soviet Union has established diplomatic ties with New China. Seventy-seven years on, the Russia-China relationship has been elevated into comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era. At this pivotal juncture, what’s China’s expectation on Russia-China relations in the future? Guo Jiakun: After 77 years of going through winds and rains together, China and Russia are all the more committed to lasting good-neighborliness and friendship, comprehensive strategic coordination, and mutual benefit and win-win cooperation in their bilateral ties, setting a stellar example of a new type of international relations. President Xi Jinping and President Vladimir Putin met twice this year in Beijing in May and in Bishkek in August, leading China-Russia relations into a new stage with higher-quality and faster development. We are confident that, under the guidance of the two leaders, China and Russia will remain true to the founding vision of the diplomatic ties and deepen our comprehensive strategic coordination. We will make advancing the development and revitalization of our respective countries an important mission, and shoulder our responsibilities as major countries by reforming and improving global governance, so as to open up an even broader prospect for China-Russia relations. Phoenix TV: It is reported that Japan’s defense minister Shinjiro Koizumi reiterated on Monday that during the revision of the three security documents, discussions on the possession of nuclear weapons and nuclear submarines should not be ruled out. He claimed that discussions should be made “without taboo” or predetermined results; and if discussions are not even allowed, it will be “a bit at odds with my sense of crisis.” What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: The possession of nuclear weapons is not an issue that Japan can “allow discussion” if it wants to. Japan is a non-nuclear-weapon state party to the Non-Proliferation Treaty and therefore has a bounden duty under international law to not receive, manufacture, acquire or transfer nuclear weapons. There is no room for negotiation. Just last February, Sanae Takaichi reiterated Japan’s commitment to the three non-nuclear principles. Japan’s representative reaffirmed multiple times at the Review Conference of the Parties to the NPT in May that the three non-nuclear principles would not be changed. Their words still ring in our ears. The “no-nuclear-taboo” remark by the incumbent head of Japan’s defense establishment is a blatant provocation and serious stomp on the NPT and the postwar international order. It is diametrically opposed to the three non-nuclear principles that Japan claims to uphold. His remark once again revealed the Japanese right-wing pursuit of a nuclear Japan. In recent years, Japan has been accelerating remilitarization and attempting to revise the three non-nuclear principles by strengthening the so-called “extended deterrence” arrangement, seeking nuclear weapon deployment in Japan, attempting to progressively ease nuclear restrictions, and challenging the red line drawn by the international community. This year marks 80 years of the opening of the Tokyo Trials. History has not and will not forget the calamities brought by Japanese militarism onto the people in Asia and elsewhere in the world. As Japanese right-wing forces keep challenging the postwar international order and the non-proliferation regime and moving further down the wrong path, the international community needs to call on Japan to strictly observe the three non-nuclear principles, fulfill its obligations under the NPT, abandon remilitarization and nuclear attempt, and earnestly respond to the concerns of the international community. **************************************** The following question was raised after the press conference: The first meeting of the 9th State Duma was held today. Candidate from the United Russia party Vyacheslav Volodin was elected as the new chairman of the State Duma. What is China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China congratulates Russia on the successful election of the ninth State Duma. Chairman of the NPC Standing Committee Zhao Leji has congratulated Chairman Vyacheslav Volodin right after his election. Cooperation between legislative bodies is part and parcel of the China-Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination for the new era. China stands ready to fully work with Russia to deliver on the important common understandings between the presidents of the two countries, further deepen exchanges and cooperation between the two state legislatures and enrich the substance of China-Russia relations. During the National Day holiday, there will be no regular press conference from October 1 to 7. The regular press conference will resume on October 8. During this period, questions can be submitted to the Spokesperson’s Office via fax, E-mail or WeChat.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 29, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
CCTV: Today marks the 54th anniversary of the issuance of the China-Japan Joint Statement. As China-Japan relations face grave difficulties, how does China see the historical significance of the four political documents between the two countries, including the joint statement, and how are they still relevant today? Guo Jiakun: Today 54 years ago, the older generation of Chinese and Japanese leaders, with extraordinary political vision and courage, signed and issued the China-Japan Joint Statement, which marked the normalization of relations between the two countries. In the joint statement, Japan explicitly noted that it is “keenly conscious of” and “deeply reproaches itself” over its responsibility for war and that it “recognizes the Government of the People’s Republic of China as the sole legal Government of China.” The statement also notes that the Government of Japan “fully understands and respects” the position of the Chinese government that Taiwan is an inalienable part of the territory of the People’s Republic of China. The four political documents between China and Japan, including the joint statement, laid the political and legal foundation for China-Japan relations, and established the rules for properly settling major issues of principle, including history and Taiwan. There should be no distortion or regression, still less sabotage, regarding these principles. Today, more than half a century later, China-Japan relations once again face a severe situation. The root cause is that the political foundation of the bilateral relations has been gravely undermined. The incumbent leader of Japan not only refuses to reflect on the history of aggression, but also claims that a contingency in Taiwan will constitute a “survival threatening” situation for Japan. This is a blatant challenge to China’s state sovereignty and against the aspiration demonstrated by the normalization of China-Japan relations and the political commitments Japan made to China. Japan keeps peddling the so-called “external threat” narrative, using it as a pretext to speed up remilitarization. The move poses a challenge to the postwar international order and threatens regional peace and stability. History has repeatedly shown that only by staying true to the spirit of the four political documents can China and Japan keep the relationship on the right course. Just as Foreign Minister Wang Yi noted in the meeting yesterday with Takeshi Iwaya, head of the Japanese Association for the Promotion of International Trade, the pressing priority for Japan is to correct Japanese leader’s erroneous words and deeds on the Taiwan question. Japan should adopt a correct attitude on historical issues, and form an objective and rational perception on China. On this day of historic significance, we once again urge those running the government of Japan to seriously reflect on and correct their wrongdoings, and take real actions to return to the purpose and mission of the four political documents. TASS: The spokesperson of Kremlin expressed that the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting in Shenzhen will provide a good opportunity for a trilateral meeting of leaders of Russia, China and the U.S. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: As this year’s host of APEC, China stands ready to work with all parties for fruitful outcomes of the APEC “China Year,” and contribute to the economic growth in the Asia Pacific and beyond. For your question, I have no information to share at the moment. Shenzhen TV: It’s reported that the Philippine National Maritime Council on September 25 unveiled an updated maritime chart, which includes islands and reefs in China’s Nansha Qundao such as Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao. What’s China’s comment? Guo Jiakun: Zhongye Dao and Mahuan Dao are part of China’s Nansha Qundao and Chinese territory. China has indisputable sovereignty over Nansha Qundao and its adjacent waters. The scope of Philippine territory is defined by several international treaties. China’s Nanhai Zhudao, including Nansha Qundao, lie beyond that scope. The Philippines’ illegal occupation of several islands and reefs in Nansha Qundao, designation of so-called “Kalayaan Island Group” beyond its own territory, and so-called “maritime chart,” which includes relevant islands and reefs of China’s Nansha Qundao, seriously violate China’s territorial sovereignty and the UN Charter and relevant international laws. Those actions are illegal, null and void. China firmly opposes any action of the Philippines that harms China’s sovereignty and rights and interests. China will continue taking necessary measures to firmly defend its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests in the South China Sea.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 28, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-28
CCTV: President Xi Jinping’s state visit to the U.S. last week drew close international attention. Can you share more information on this visit? Guo Jiakun: From September 23 to 25, at the invitation of President Trump, President Xi Jinping paid a successful state visit to the U.S. The two presidents had in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development. They reached a number of important common understandings on building “a constructive relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity.” Both sides agreed to support each other in successfully hosting the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting and G20 Summit this year. China stands ready to work with the U.S. to deliver on the important common understandings between the two presidents and promote the steady, sound and sustainable development of China-U.S. relations. Xinhua News Agency: A few days ago, China successfully hosted the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the UN headquarters in New York. President Xi Jinping sent a congratulatory letter to event. Vice President Han Zheng attended the event and delivered remarks. The event was also attended by many state leaders, ministers, and heads of international organizations. Could you tell us more about the high-level dialogue? Guo Jiakun: On September 25, the High-level Dialogue on the Fifth Anniversary of the Global Development Initiative was successfully held at the UN headquarters in New York. More than 300 guests, including leaders and ministerial officials from member states of the Group of Friends of the GDI and heads of international organizations, attended the event. In his congratulatory letter, President Xi Jinping noted that the GDI was proposed to advance global development cooperation, reinvigorate the global development cause, and help accelerate the implementation of the UN 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development. Over the past five years, with the joint efforts of all parties, cooperation projects under the initiative have taken root and yielded outcomes in more than 120 countries. China stands ready to work with all parties to uphold a people-centered development philosophy and strive for more substantive progress in implementing the GDI. Vice President Han Zheng attended the high-level dialogue. In his remarks, he elaborated on the great significance of the GDI and put forward four proposals: First, we should strengthen solidarity and coordination to fully implement the SDGs. China will continue to support the UN in strengthening the development pillar. Second, we should stay action-oriented and actively pursue development that benefits the people. China will train 10,000 engineers for developing countries over the next five years. Third, we should expand cooperation in priority areas and accelerate empowerment-driven development. China is ready to work with all parties to implement flagship projects under the GDI, including “Digital South” and “Clean Stove.” Fourth, we should strengthen partnerships to promote interconnected development. China will conduct extensive cooperation through relevant bilateral, trilateral and multilateral mechanisms to create synergy. The substantive actions and fruitful outcomes of the GDI over the past five years speak volumes about China’s commitment to human progress and world harmony, as well as its efforts to offer China’s solutions and make China’s contributions to the common development for all countries. China stands ready to work with all parties to continuously turn the vision of the SDGs into tangible reality and to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity. Anadolu Agency: One of the outcomes of the U.S.-China summit was that the two sides agreed on establishing an artificial intelligence dialogue. Do you think this bilateral mechanism will be a sufficient framework for global AI governance? Guo Jiakun: China takes a constructive and responsible part in global AI governance and acts as a solution contributor to the process. China stands for upholding the UN’s role as the main channel and building a fair and equitable global AI governance system. We are willing to maintain communication and exchanges with the U.S. through inter-governmental dialogue on AI and other channels. This is both an important pathway towards AI for good and for all, and integral to the vision of a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability on the basis of respect, fairness, and reciprocity. Prensa Latina: Today marks the 66th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between Cuba and China. How does China view its relationship with Cuba nowadays amid turbulent international situations, even though both countries have always maintained strong bonds of friendship? Guo Jiakun: Since China and Cuba established the diplomatic relations 66 years ago, the two countries have maintained a deep friendship from generation to generation. In recent years, under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, sustained and steady progress has been made in building a community with a shared future between China and Cuba. No matter how the international landscape evolves, China will firmly support Cuba in exploring the socialist development path suited to its national conditions and in safeguarding national sovereignty and opposing external interference. Yonhap News Agency: The Chinese side said in a readout that Chinese and U.S. presidents exchanged views on the Korean Peninsula issue in their meetings. Could you elaborate on that? Guo Jiakun: During the visit, the two presidents exchanged views on major international and regional issues of mutual interest. China’s position and policy on the Korean Peninsula issue maintains consistency and continuity. Bloomberg: Scott Bessent said that China came up with the idea, proposed a bigger deal between the two countries, and that the U.S. was willing to entertain that bigger deal or continue on with the Busan arrangement. Can you confirm that China did indeed offer or propose a bigger deal and maybe describe what that bigger deal might entertain? Guo Jiakun: Competent authorities have shared information on the eighth round of China-U.S. economic and trade consultations. I’d refer you to them for more details. Global Times: Several permanent missions to the UN have told the media that China is weighing whether to support UNCTAD Secretary-General and former Vice President of Costa Rica Rebeca Grynspan or Guyana’s Permanent Representative to the UN Carolyn Rodrigues-Birkett in the vote for the new UN Secretary-General. Can you confirm this? Which candidate is China considering supporting? Guo Jiakun: The election of UN Secretary-General bears on the reform and development of the UN and the vital interests of member states. China supports the selection in accordance with the UN Charter of a new Secretary-General who observes the UN Charter, shows outstanding competence, is impartial and upright, and fulfills responsibilities with dedication. China will work with all relevant parties to participate in the election process in a responsible manner. DPA: The German federal government commissioner for culture and the media said that on TikTok, Europe should “follow the American example,” it is dangerous to Europe’s democracy if other countries have the sensitive information, and TikTok’s European business should be “in European hands.” What is the foreign ministry’s comment? Guo Jiakun: China’s position on TikTok is consistent and clear.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson’s Remarks on Issue Concerning Artificial Intelligence
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-26
Q: In the U.S. readout on the outcomes of the just concluded state visit, we noted the use of “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence.” How does China see this? A: The two presidents had in-depth discussion on AI during this visit. On what term to use for artificial intelligence, China attaches importance to the position of the U.S. side and respects their choice of the term. The advancement of artificial intelligence is an ongoing process. Parties can have more communication and in-depth exchange of views to seek consensus in light of how the process may evolve.

item.title: Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Guo Jiakun’s Regular Press Conference on September 24, 2026
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-24
CGTN: We’ve noted that the fifth Global Digital Trade Expo (GDTE) opened in Hangzhou this morning under the theme “Meet the AI Future at GDTE.” Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Can you share more information on that? Guo Jiakun: This morning, the fifth GDTE opened in Hangzhou. Premier Li Qiang attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Leaders including Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim and Chairman of the Cabinet of Ministers of Kyrgyzstan Adylbek Aleshovich Kasymaliev attended and addressed the launching ceremony. Other leaders including Director General of the UN Industrial Development Organization Gerd Müller addressed the event via video link. Over 1,200 representatives from various sectors of close to 50 countries and regions and relevant international organizations attended the launching ceremony. In response to questions such as where global trade is heading amid the trend of digitalization, what should the world do to capitalize on that trend, and what role can China play, Premier Li Qiang shared three observations. First, the need to grasp the new changes and new trends in global trade through digital trade. Flourishing digital trade provides new impetus and opportunities. The world economy faces broad prospects as well as new development gaps. Market matching becomes more convenient while at the same time, new trade barriers emerge. Global trade can accelerate growth through innovation, but without sufficient protection of relevant rules. Second, openness is essential to enable better development of global trade in the digital era. Amid economic globalization, the international community needs to engage in sincere coordination. We need to enhance digital connectivity for more free trade, bridge the digital divide for more universally beneficial trade, and improve digital governance for more orderly trade. Third, China will make greater contribution to global digital trade. We will keep expanding digital consumer demand and share market opportunities with countries around the world. We will continue to strengthen support for the digital industry and empower global digitalization. China’s technology advancement follows an open-source approach such as in the field of artificial intelligence to build “digital ladders” accessible to all countries. We will continue to improve the environment for digital development and offer China’s solutions to setting up well-rounded international rules. Foreign leaders noted in their remarks that the the GDTE provides an invaluable platform for countries to have discussions on cooperation, jointly promote development and share outcomes. They appreciated China’s effort of sharing development outcomes and expressed hopes to work with China to bridge the digital divide, build a fair, safe and secure global digital trade order for good and for all, and provide new impetus for the sustainable development of the world. The fifth GDTE coincides with the joyous occasion of the Mid-Autumn Festival. We welcome friends from the press to cover this event and feel the vibe of cutting-edge technology in Hangzhou. Reuters: The U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the U.S. and China have reached a deal to extend the current trade truce all the way to January 10. China has so far not released any information about this. Has China agreed to this two-month extension? Guo Jiakun: I’d refer you to competent authorities for any specifics regarding the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues. Bloomberg: The Iranian president said during a UN address that his country won’t allow freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz while sanctions and a U.S. blockade remain in place. We’re wondering if the foreign ministry has any comment on his remarks. Guo Jiakun: Protraction of the U.S.-Iran conflict does not serve the common interests of the parties concerned or the international community. It is vital for parties to choose peace, resolve disputes through dialogue and negotiation, and restore peace and tranquility to the Middle East and Gulf region at an early date. The New York Times: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that China and the U.S. agreed to set up a formalized dialogue on AI that includes an incident line for communicating about AI safety incidents. Can MOFA confirm whether China has agreed to this dialogue and this notification system? Guo Jiakun: The Chinese side has released a readout on the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues, which you may refer to. For further information, I’d refer you to competent authorities. NHK: It has been almost a month since Gyirong County was hit by the devastating mudslide. Could you provide the latest casualty figures for foreign nationals and an update on the rescue operations? Guo Jiakun: The disaster left 261 foreign nationals unaccounted for. China has shared information with their countries’ embassies in Beijing. Reuters: New Zealand’s cyber security agency said China was the country’s most persistent and capable state-backed cyber threat. What is the ministry’s comment of this? Guo Jiakun: China opposes and resolutely fights hacker attacks in accordance with law, and opposes the dissemination of cyber security disinformation for political purposes. China urges the relevant agency in New Zealand to stop spreading lies and stoking discord, and instead do more to foster mutual understanding and trust between the two countries. The New York Times: Are further trade talks planned between the United States and China on the sidelines of the APEC finance ministers’ meeting in Hong Kong in October, or in conjunction with the APEC summit in Shenzhen? Has China formally invited Mr. Trump to the Shenzhen summit? Guo Jiakun: On questions related to the China-U.S. consultations on economic and trade issues, I’d refer you to competent authorities. On your second question, China and the U.S. are in communication regarding interactions between the two presidents within the year. ******************************************************** During the Mid-Autumn Festival, there will be no regular press conference on September 25. The regular press conference will resume on September 28. During this period, questions can be submitted to the Spokesperson’s Office via fax, E-mail or WeChat. We wish you and your family a happy Mid-Autumn Festival!
